classification.difficultyReason: Combine Pythagoras with triangular cross-section area, enumerate all five prism faces and preserve exact surd before the volume product; select and connect familiar methods.

content.prompt: Find the surface area and volume of the prism shown below. The cross-section is a right-angled isosceles triangle.

spec.description: Right-isosceles triangular prism with both perpendicular cross-section legs4cm and depth12cm, source two right-angle cues, explicit convex face model/view and derived hidden edges.
spec.mathematics: Right-isosceles triangular prism with both perpendicular cross-section legs4cm and depth12cm, source two right-angle cues, explicit convex face model/view and derived hidden edges.
spec.answerVisibility: Source givens only; derived area/volume not printed.

answer.worked:
The triangular cross-section has area $A=\frac12(4)(4)=8\text{ cm}^2$. Pythagoras gives hypotenuse $\sqrt{4^2+4^2}=4\sqrt2\text{ cm}$. Add the two triangular and three rectangular faces:
$$S=2(8)+12(4+4+4\sqrt2)=112+48\sqrt2=16(7+3\sqrt2)\text{ cm}^2.$$
The volume is $V=Ah=8(12)=96\text{ cm}^3$.
